# `go/doc/comment` test corpus

Copied from `$GOROOT/src/go/doc/comment/testdata` (go1.26.5).

[txtar](https://pkg.go.dev/golang.org/x/tools/txtar) format. `-- input --` is
the parser input; each following `-- name --` section is the expected output
of one `comment.Printer` method.

`tests/doc_comment.rs` checks the **`gofmt`** sections — `Printer.Comment`,
the only printer `go/printer`'s `formatDocComment` calls, and the only one
ported. It asserts that every file here has a `gofmt` section, so a fixture
that would silently test nothing fails instead.

18 of the 53 files upstream ships with no `gofmt` section (they exercise only
`html`, `markdown` or `text`). Rather than delete them — which would have
thrown away 18 parser inputs — the section was generated by running
go1.26.5's own `comment.Printer.Comment` over each file's `input`:

    go run scripts/gen-doccomment-gofmt-sections.go \
        crates/guff-ast/tests/testdata/doc_comment

So every expectation here is upstream's answer, whether upstream shipped it or
the script asked for it. The `html`, `markdown`, `text` and `dump` sections are
kept as-is: they are upstream's artifacts, and deleting them would make a later
port of those printers re-derive a corpus that already exists.
